preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of edges m is at least n-1 and at most the minimum of 300,000 or the maximum possible edges in a simple graph.
The number of special vertices k is between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(special_vertices) == k and len(set(special_vertices)) == k and all(1 <= v <= n for v in special_vertices)
preconditions.description: There are exactly k distinct special vertices, each with an index between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: len(c) == n and all(0 <= x <= 10**9 for x in c)
preconditions.description: The list of vertex rewards c has length n, with each value between 0 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(w) == m and all(0 <= x <= 10**9 for x in w)
preconditions.description: The list of edge costs w has length m, with each value between 0 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == m and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: There are m edges, each connecting two distinct vertices within the valid range.

preconditions.expression: len(set(tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges)) == m
preconditions.description: There is at most one edge between any pair of vertices (no duplicate edges).
The undirected graph formed by the edges is connected.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in output_values)
postconditions.description: Each output value is an integer.

postconditions.expression: all(output_values[i] == max_profit_for_target(i + 1, n, m, k, special_vertices, c, w, edges) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each vertex i (1-indexed), the i-th output value is the maximum possible profit achievable when vertex i is required to be saturated. The profit is defined as the sum of rewards for all saturated vertices minus the sum of costs for all undirected edges, where a vertex is saturated if it is reachable from every special vertex in the resulting directed/undirected graph.
